newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commissioners 'should be fined' for poor performance-MEP.
newsitem.headline: Commissioners 'should be fined' for poor performance-MEP.

text.p: The European Commissioners should lose 10 percent of their salaries unless they improve financial control in the Commission, a member of European Parliament budget committee said on Thursday.

"I will propose to put a certain percentage of Commissioners' salaries in the (budget) reserve until we have go a clear explanation of some of the problems," Laurens Brinkhorst, the parliament's rapporteur on the European Union's 1997 budget, told reporters on Thursday.
MEPs were concerned about "cases of mismanagement", especially in the Commission's Directorate General for tourism and small and medium enterprises, the Dutch Liberal explained.
Parliament's budget committee, which is currently finalising its position on the 1997 budget, is expected to endorse Brinkhorst's pay-freeze proposal on Thursday night.
The full parliament will give the draft budget a first reading on October 24.

If Parliament approves Brinkhorst's plan and the Commissioners take no satisfactory action by the time of the budget's second reading in December, they could each lose 54,000 Belgian Francs a month from next January onwards.
"We want to send a political signal that the body as a whole must take this question seriously," Brinkhorst said.
Budget committee chairman Detlev Samland said further confrontation was brewing, this time between parliament and the Council, who share joint control over the EU budget.

Unless EU finance ministers agreed on October 14 to raise the EU's forecast spending limit by one billion Ecus, the parliament would probably refuse to approve Council's request to allocate 352 million Ecus to trans-European transport networks, the German Socialist said.

Parliament would also refuse to approve a 1.8-billion-Ecu package to help beef farmers cope with the BSE (mad cow) crisis if Council did not produce acceptable proposals for financing the plan in time, he added.

The budget committee supported Council's decision to cut payments from the Structural Funds by one billion Ecus in 1997 but other MEPs might challenge this decision on October 24, a committee official told Reuters.
The committee is due to finish its examination of the draft budget on Friday.
